# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.


---

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.


---

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.


---

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.


---

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.


---

# Scenario 10: the power goes off

A release harness is killed mid-attempt (power cut, OOM, `kill -9`, laptop closed) and started again. This scenario states what must be true after the restart. It does not say how; a variant that satisfies every line by any mechanism passes, and its design.md must name the mechanism and what the harness author had to write for it.

## Must express

- Kind Release, supplied by the operator. Its flow, in order: `build` (a command that is safe to run twice), `announce` (a command that posts a message to a channel; posting twice is wrong), `review` (an agent on a model), `approval` (a halt for a release manager), `summarize` (a model call submitted to a batch API and collected later), then it spawns one Smoke unit per platform in a `smoke` lane and waits for them.
- After a restart, a step that completed before the crash is not run again and costs nothing.
- The step that was running at the crash is handled per step, declared by the harness author on the step or the command: rerun it (`build`), never rerun it and park the attempt for the supervisor (`announce`, unless the harness can tell that the post happened, in which case it continues), or ask the step's driver whether it finished (`review`: the agent's session may have completed while the harness was down).
- An `approval` halt resolved while the harness was down is found on restart and the flow continues from it.
- A `summarize` batch submitted before the crash is collected, not resubmitted.
- A resumed attempt is the same attempt: one id, one row in every metric, and the crash is never counted as a model failure or an agent failure.
- Smoke children that finished while the parent was down are seen by the parent on restart; children still running are not restarted.
- An attempt whose flow definition changed between the crash and the restart (a step renamed, a step inserted before the one that was running) is not silently rerun. It is parked for the supervisor with a reason, and the supervisor can restart it from the top or abandon it.
- The harness author writes no resumption code: no checkpoint, no "if already done" branch in a flow, no reading of the ledger from a flow.
- Two copies of the harness started against the same ledger by mistake: the second refuses to start, or takes over from a dead first, and never both run.

## Hostile aspects

- Effects of three kinds (safe to repeat, wrong to repeat, outside the harness's control) in one flow, each with its own restart behaviour, declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- State that moved while the harness was down (a halt resolved, a batch completed, a child finished) and must be found, not replayed from memory.
- A definition that changed under a running attempt.
- Single-writer exclusion over a shared ledger.
- Everything above must hold with the ledger as the only kernel state (principle 15), and the author must have nothing to write for it (principle 2).


---

# Scenario 11: halts with a clock, and retries with a bound

A contracts harness: an agent drafts, outside counsel reviews, finance signs off. Drafted for run two from the generation 1 and 2 critiques; every requirement here was a gap two or more adversaries found independently.

## Must express

- Kind Contract, supplied by a webhook (new contracts and counterparty redlines on existing ones) and by the operator. State in the document system via its API. Flow: `draft` (agent), halt `counsel` (outside counsel, days), halt `signoff` (finance), `execute` (command that is wrong to repeat).
- **Bounded retry as a lane policy.** A failed attempt retries under a policy declared on the lane, not on the kind: `contracts-eu` retries three times with exponential backoff, `contracts-us` retries once; both lanes handle the same kind. When the policy is exhausted the unit moves where the kind says, and nowhere else. A kind with no declared move and an exhausted policy is a startup error, not an infinite loop.
- **A halt with a clock.** If finance does not answer `signoff` within 30 minutes, the halt resolves itself to "approve under $500, else reject", recorded as resolved by timeout, distinct from a human resolution and from a policy resolution. The same attempt continues; nothing is cancelled or restarted. The 30 minutes are measured from the recorded halt, never from a field in unit data or from unit creation; at 20 minutes a deputy is paged and either person may resolve.
- **A policy-resolved halt is a policy.** Contracts in a category with 200 approved samples and zero rejections skip `counsel`. The skip is a registered policy with a recorded decision carrying the metric it read and its sample count, not a predicate inline in the handler.
- **Scoped resolvers.** Counsel resolves `counsel` through a plain HTTP dashboard and nothing else. Finance resolves `signoff` through a Claude Code supervisor and nothing else. An auditor client reads every decision and resolves none. The grant names the halt, not a capability string.
- **Waiting holds no capacity.** Drafting WIP is 3. Forty contracts awaiting counsel consume none of it and are not active on the board.
- **Returns bounded without ledger reads in the flow.** Counsel may return a contract; after the second return the unit ends in Declined, a failure. The flow contains no count of returns and reads nothing from the ledger; the bound is declared.
- **An event mid-attempt is neither dropped nor fatal.** A redline arriving while `draft` runs does not cancel the attempt and is not lost; it is applied in the next round. A redline arriving while the unit waits on counsel re-enters the flow at `draft`.
- Metrics: median time to decision per halt and per resolver, with sample counts; retries per lane this month; share of `signoff` halts resolved by timeout.

## Hostile aspects

- A retry policy that lives on the lane and differs per lane for one kind, with a declared end.
- A timer that resolves a halt instead of cancelling an attempt, and a third resolver kind beside human and policy.
- A halt as an entity that grants, metrics, timers and policies all reference by identity, never by string.
- Two clients on two transports with disjoint rights over the same unit.
- Position honesty: a unit waiting on a human is at `waiting`, holds no WIP, and the board says so.
- A bound on re-entries that the author declares and the kernel enforces, with no attempt arithmetic in the flow.


---

# Scenario 12: long external jobs, and work under locks

An ML platform team. Drafted for run two from the generation 2 and 3 critiques: long external effects that are neither model, human nor batch; and shared-database maintenance, proposed in two generations by independent adversaries.

## Must express

- Kind EvalRun, supplied by the operator, stored in the harness store. Flow: `prepare` (command), `submit` (a command that hands a job to an external GPU service and gets a job id; the job runs 2 to 8 hours), `collect` (the result, polled every 10 minutes), `score` (command), `summarize` (model).
- While the job runs the unit holds no WIP and no runner slot; the lane has WIP 2 and keeps starting new runs. On restart a submitted job is collected, not resubmitted. A job failing remotely is an attempt failure; a harness crash while it runs is not.
- Kind Migration, supplied from a folder of migration files in order. Each takes an exclusive lock on one named database; two migrations on one database never overlap, migrations on different databases run concurrently. A migration is wrong to repeat: after a crash mid-migration the attempt is parked for the supervisor with what was recorded, never rerun.
- Kind Backfill, supplied by the operator, one unit per table, in batches of 10,000 rows. A backfill takes a shared lock on its database that a Migration's exclusive lock excludes and is excluded by. A backfill interrupted by a crash resumes at the next batch, not the first; the author writes no checkpoint.
- Ordering across units: migration 0042 must not start before 0041 has succeeded, whatever order the folder is read in; a failed 0041 parks 0042 with a reason.
- Metrics: hours of GPU jobs in flight per day with sample counts; lock wait time per database.

## Hostile aspects

- An external effect with submit and collect semantics, in the kernel's vocabulary, holding no capacity while it runs.
- Locks on named resources shared by kinds, exclusive and shared, with the lease as kernel state and the resource as an entity.
- Non-idempotent effects whose restart behaviour is declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- Ordering declared between units of one kind, with a parked unit carrying its reason.
- Batch-shaped resumption inside one attempt without checkpoint code in the flow.


# Judging rubric

Judges compare two variants, A and B, and name a winner on one criterion. Never score in isolation. Never reward length or completeness of prose. Prefer the variant a stranger could use correctly after reading its scenario files once.

## Criteria (one comparison per criterion)

- **fidelity**: which variant violates fewer principles in `principles.md`, and violates none of 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11? Each violation is a strike; a strike on a dividing-line principle counts double.
- **ergonomics**: in the scenario files, which variant lets a reader predict each line's effect from its name, keeps builder chains consistent, and needs fewer things explained?
- **expressiveness**: across the battery, which variant expresses the scenarios with fewer workarounds, fewer raw strings standing in for entities, and no lies (mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean)?
- **economy**: which variant achieves the same coverage with a smaller surface: fewer entities, fewer methods, no one-use entity, no unused method?
- **connectedness**: which variant's entities connect through named pivots, with no orphan concept, no hidden coupling (a flow that secretly knows another kind, a role that knows a vendor), and no two words for one thing?

## Framings (each comparison is asked under one framing)

- **laravel**: you maintain a framework loved for striking the line between what it decides and what it leaves open. Judge whether the variant decides the right things.
- **durable**: you build durable-execution engines (Temporal, Step Functions). Judge whether the execution model (attempts, re-entry, cancellation, blocked, spawn) will survive contact with real failures.
- **newcomer**: you have never seen harness-dsl. You must implement the scenario named in the prompt tonight. Judge which variant you would rather be handed.
- **owner**: judge strictly against `principles.md`, nothing else.
- **adversary**: for each variant, find the scenario in the battery it handles worst, and judge which variant's worst case is less bad.

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else:

{"winner": "A" | "B", "confidence": 0.5-1.0, "reasons": ["...", "..."]}

Reasons are specific: quote the line or name that decided it. At most three.


# Known weaknesses of the owner's own seed

# Known weaknesses of the owner's seed (ours-2, as of 2026-11-01 after run one)

Fed to the adversary as "known; find what we did not see", and to mutation as targets.

1. **Seat and agent overlap.** An agent is "a seat with one model"; two nouns for one pivot unless the seat earns its place in every scenario that compares models.
2. **Job and batch overlap.** A batch of model calls is a submit-and-collect job; two step kinds where one may do.
3. **Halt as an entity and halt as a step.** `H.halt(name)` is referenced by identity, but a flow may halt at the same question twice; the address of a halt in a flow and the halt entity are two things.
4. **Resources map to adapters.** `H.resource('edge')` is pure name; the lease plugin maps it to globs. Two harnesses may map one resource differently, and nothing checks the mapping covers every resource the kinds touch.
5. **Pool serves models.** `pool.serves(...models)` is a relationship on an instance; whether it belongs on the pool, the model or a named pivot is undecided.
6. **Retry bound on the lane, exit map on the lane.** The lane now carries kind, suppliers, store, handler, exits, retry, WIP and ceiling; the adversaries called a lane with eight concerns overloaded.
7. **Multi-attempt units.** An Epic that spawns and re-enters, a Negotiation of many rounds: the flow re-enters from the top and must find where it is from recorded results; whether that needs a `loopback` pivot, as one evolved variant has, is open.
8. **The supervisor's client hides its transport**, still; two supervisors on one session (scenario 7) have no entity.
9. **Startup validation is listed, not specified.** Name collisions, exits outside the kind's states, a trigger on an unregistered lane, a facet repeating a column, an agent no pool serves: all should fail at `start()`.
10. **Memory capture** is a trigger consequence (`journal.record`); nothing turns outcomes into candidate memories without an author writing the trigger.

# harness-dsl: minimal, cut again (child of g01-minimal-imal-0-2)

The operator for this child is surface-cut. It applies three changes:

- It removes methods, fields and options that the battery never reads, or that have one caller and can be a default.
- It repairs the adversary's three sharpest critiques. Two of the repairs also delete surface.
- It fixes the principle-12 gap the parent left open.

Scenarios 11 and 12 (run two) then forced a second, additive pass. That pass is recorded at the end of "What changed and why".

## Entities

| Sort | Entity | Builder | Produces / is |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind | **state** | `H.state(name, position)`, or `H.state(name, 'terminal', verdict)` | A shareable lifecycle position. |
| Kind | **kind** | `H.kind(n).data(z).states(initial, ...others)` | A data shape and a set of states. |
| Kind | **role** | `H.role(n).input(z).output(z).prompt(f).intents([...])` | What a model call is asked to do. |
| Kind | **memory** | `H.memory(n, 'experience' \| 'taste')` | A memory kind. |
| Kind | **halt** | `H.halt(n, decision).about(z).timeout(after, resolve).policy(rule)` | A named outside decision. It declares what is asked, the shape of the answer, the facts it is raised with, and optionally a clock resolver and a policy resolver. |
| Kind | **resource** | `H.resource(n)` | A named shared thing that locks reference by identity. |
| Instance | account, model, runner, store, memory store, supplier, ledger, guard, observer, client | adapters only | Specific resources, each with its backend. |
| Pivot | **agent** | `H.agent(n, role).model(m \| policy)` | An executable: role × model. |
| Pivot | **lane** | `H.lane(n, kind).handler(flow).suppliers().store().wip().maxUsdPerUnit().retry(policy, exhausted).locks(f).after(f, onFailure)` | A work queue: kind × suppliers × store × handler, with its capacity and ordering. |
| Pivot | **library** | `H.library(n, memory, store)` | A recall source: memory kind × store. |
| Pivot | **pool** | `H.pool(n, members, policy?)` | The account that serves a call. |
| Pivot | **trigger** | `H.trigger(n, source, (event, act) => effects)` | A recorded consequence of recorded state. |
| Composite | **flow** | `H.flow(n).for(k1, k2?).params(z).does(ctx => state)` | A handler body. |
| Composite | **command** | `H.command(n).input(z).output(z).argv(f).on(...runners).recovery(r)` | A deterministic executable. |
| Composite | **job** | `H.job(n).output(z).submit(command).collect(command, every)` | An external executable: submitted now, polled until done, holding no capacity in between. |
| Composite | **policy** | `H.policy.{model, account, scheduler, retry, rule}` | A deterministic decision. |
| Composite | **operation** | `H.ops.*`, `H.ops.resolve(...halts)`, `H.operation(n, exec)` | A grantable unit of the control API. |
| Root | **harness** | `H.harness(n).ledger().lanes().pools().triggers().scheduler().clients().observers()` | The running thing. |

These are values, not entities:

- `H.clock(...)` and `H.operator`, which are kernel suppliers.
- `H.env(name)`.
- `TimeSpec`, `Interval`, `Bound`, `MetricBounds`, `Lock`, `JobPoll`.
- `SupplyOf<K>`.
- `Children<T,S>`, the handle returned by `ctx.spawn`.

## Execution vocabulary

- **Run**: one lifetime of a harness process.
- **Attempt**: one execution of a lane's flow for one unit.
  - Its states are `running`, `blocked` (on a halt), `waiting` (in `ctx.wait`, or on a job or batch) and `ended`.
  - When ended, its outcome is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- **Invocation**: one call of one executable inside an attempt.
  - Each retry and each batch item is its own invocation.
  - A job is one invocation, however many polls it takes.
- **Step** is not a word in this design.

## Rules

### 1. Skeleton (principle 12)

**Positions.** A unit has one of four positions:

| Condition | Position |
|---|---|
| A live attempt is running | `active` |
| A live attempt is blocked, waiting, or in a job or batch | `waiting` |
| No live attempt | The position its state declares |

The board and the scheduler read this position. Waiting on a human is recorded once, as the attempt's blocked state. No kind declares a state for it.

**Verdicts.** Each terminal state declares `success`, `failure` or `neutral`. The overload without a verdict does not type-check for terminal states.

**How a flow ends.**

| How the flow ends | Attempt outcome | What happens to the unit |
|---|---|---|
| Returns a state | `succeeded` | Moves to that state. |
| Returns `ctx.fail(reason)` or throws | `failed` | See the failure rule below. |
| Interrupted by an outside move, a preemption or a cost ceiling | `cancelled` | Handled by the rule that interrupted it. |

**The failure rule.**

- A failed attempt leaves the unit at pending under the lane's retry policy.
- `lane.retry(policy, exhausted)` declares that policy. When the policy returns `'stop'`, the unit moves to `exhausted`, which is a state of the lane's kind, and nowhere else.
- The kernel appends `attempt` entries with status `retrying` or `exhausted`.
- A lane without `.retry` uses the kernel default: exponential backoff from 1 minute, capped at 1 hour, with no limit. That default never exhausts, so it needs no end state.
- Because `exhausted` is a required argument, a bounded policy with no end state cannot be written.
- `KindDescriptor.failsTo` is kept for scenarios 1–10 only. See "Principles broken".

**Returning a waiting state.** The flow parks the unit with no wake time. A supply, trigger or operation must move it.

### 2. Durable waits

`ctx.wait(waitingState, { at })` and `ctx.wait(waitingState, { children })` suspend the attempt inside the flow:

- The unit moves to the waiting state.
- The attempt holds no runner slot and no WIP.
- On wake, the same attempt resumes by replay.

An attempt's `durationMs` excludes time spent blocked and waiting.

### 3. Success rate

- `successRate(kind)` is `success / (success + failure)` over terminal transitions.
- Neutral states are excluded from it, and stay countable by name.
- Every rate carries `hits` and `samples`. `value` is `null` when `samples` is 0.

### 4. Moves from outside

**Default.** Moving a unit that has a live attempt (running, blocked or waiting) cancels the attempt first.

**Deferred updates.** A supply `update` marked `deferred: true` is held while the attempt is *running*. It is applied when the attempt next blocks, waits or ends:

- If the attempt is blocked or waiting at that point, the move cancels it.
- If the attempt has ended, the move applies after the end.

A redline therefore never kills a draft in progress and is never lost (scenario 11).

### 5. Supply and keys

- A `create` whose key belongs to an open unit is ignored.
- An `update` addresses the open unit with that key.
- The ledger keeps a snapshot of every unit.
- `folder.files({ key })` sets keys from file names.

### 6. Entities in filters, not strings

**Filters take descriptors.** `EntryFilter` fields take descriptors (`kind`, `lane`, `halt`, `resource`, `trigger`, `executable`).

**Halt filters.** `halt.resolved(match?)` builds a typed filter for that halt's resolutions. `match` is `Partial<D>`.

**What remains a string.** Tags stay strings.

### 7. Halts (principle 17)

**Raising a halt.** `ctx.halt(halt, show, about)` raises the halt with typed facts `about`, which are declared by `.about(schema)`.

**Resolvers.** A halt has up to three resolvers, recorded on the resolution as `resolver`:

| Resolver | How it is declared | When it acts |
|---|---|---|
| `policy` | `.policy(rule)` | At raise. A `RulePolicy<C, D \| null>` runs first. A non-null result resolves the halt at once, and the entry carries the metric reads and sample counts. `null` falls through to the human. |
| `human` | A client granted `H.ops.resolve(halt)` | When that client resolves it. A grant names halts. `H.ops.resolveHalts` grants all of them. |
| `clock` | `.timeout(after, resolve)` | At `after` from the recorded `raised` entry, if the halt is still open. It resolves the halt with `resolve(about)`. The attempt continues; nothing is cancelled. |

**Escalation.** `H.on.halted(halt, after)` is a trigger source that fires once at `after` from the raise, if the halt is still open. It is used to page a deputy with `act.run(executable, input)`.

**Measure.** `decisionMs` is the time from raise to resolution. It is available to `mean`, `median` and `sum`, filtered by `halt` and `resolver`.

### 8. Triggers

**Unit sources:**

- `on.enters(kind, state, { times? })`. With `times: n`, it fires only on a unit's n-th entry into the state. This is the declared bound on re-entries.
- `on.streak`.
- `on.deadline`.

**Other sources:**

- `on.metric`, ungrouped or grouped, with hysteresis.
- `on.halted`.

**Firing order.** Triggers whose source is a transition run in the transaction that records the transition, before the scheduler sees the unit.

**Effects:** `create`, `move`, `remember`, `pause`, `resume`, `run`.

**Recording.** Every firing is a `firing` entry.

### 9. Scheduler, capacity, locks and ordering

**Scheduler.**

- The scheduler returns an ordered `start` list and an optional `preempt` list.
- The kernel starts units in that order while lane WIP, runner slots, account eligibility, lane pause, locks and ordering allow.
- WIP and runner slots are held only by attempts at position `active`. A unit waiting on counsel, on a GPU job or in `ctx.wait` holds neither.

**Locks.** `lane.locks(data => Lock[])` declares the locks a unit takes for the life of its attempt, before it starts.

- A lock is `{ resource, mode: 'exclusive' | 'shared' }`.
- Exclusive excludes everything on that resource. Shared excludes only exclusive.
- Leases are ledger entries (`lease` requested / acquired / released), and `lockWaitMs` is measured on `acquired`.
- A blocked or waiting attempt keeps its locks. A migration paused mid-run still owns its database.

**Ordering.** `lane.after(data => predecessorKey | null, onPredecessorFailure)` holds a unit until the predecessor unit reaches a `success` terminal.

- If the predecessor ends at `failure` or `neutral`, the unit moves to `onPredecessorFailure`. That state must be a waiting state.
- The move is a transition carrying `reason`.

**Placement.** `command.on(...runners)` places an invocation on the first runner with a free slot and a passing preflight.

### 10. Jobs (principle 3)

`H.job(n).output(z).submit(cmd).collect(cmd, every)` declares a job:

- `submit` returns a handle, recorded on an `invocation` entry with status `submitted`.
- The attempt then waits: it holds no WIP and no slot.
- The kernel runs `collect(handle)` every `every` until it returns `done` or `failed`.
- A remote `failed` is an invocation failure, and therefore an attempt failure if the flow fails on it.
- On restart, a submitted job is collected, never resubmitted.
- The invocation's `durationMs` is the job's time in flight, from submit to end. Its mode is `job`.

### 11. Cost

- `maxUsdPerUnit` is cumulative across a unit's attempts.
- An invocation that would pass it blocks on the kernel halt `cost-ceiling`.

### 12. Accounts and quota (principle 15)

- Quota is a ledger partition of append-only events, folded at read time.
- `sqlite.ledger(path, { sharedQuota })` places that partition in a shared file.
- Shares belong to pools.

### 13. Memory

- The kernel owns the envelope.
- Candidates are never recalled until accepted.
- Recall is one deterministic kernel policy.

### 14. Durability (scenario 10)

**Replay.**

- Every `run`, `batch`, `job`, `halt`, `decide`, `move`, `update`, `remember`, `spawn` and `wait` is a ledger entry with a sequence number.
- After a restart, recorded results are returned without invoking again.
- A loop of batch commands (scenario 12 backfill) resumes at the first batch with no recorded result. The one that was running follows its command's `.recovery`.

**Interrupted invocations.**

- Commands follow `.recovery`: `'rerun'`, `'park'` (the default), or a check command.
- A parked attempt is blocked on the kernel halt `interrupted`, with what was recorded.

**The attempt record.**

- A resumed attempt keeps its id.
- Interrupted invocations are excluded from model and agent rates.

**A changed definition.** A changed flow fingerprint blocks the attempt on the kernel halt `definition-changed`.

**Single writer.** `start()` holds a renewed ledger lease.

### 15. Control API

- The API is made of operations.
- `claude-code.supervisor` is one client. `http.control` is a plain-HTTP client.
- Grants are per client. Two clients may hold disjoint `resolve` grants over the same unit.

### 16. Startup validation

`start()` fails in each of these cases:

- duplicate descriptor names, including halts and resources;
- a flow whose states are not states of its lane's kind;
- a `wait`, `failsTo` or `after` target whose position is wrong;
- a `retry` exhausted state that is not a state of the lane's kind;
- an unregistered lane referenced by a trigger;
- an agent that no pool can serve;
- a command without argv or runners;
- a job whose submit or collect command has no runner;
- a missing ledger;
- a batch on a model without `submit` and `collect`;
- a halt with `.timeout` or `.policy` but no `.about` when its resolver reads facts.

A harness with no pools, agents or models is valid.

## What changed and why

### Repairs of the adversary's critiques (first pass)

| Critique | Repair |
|---|---|
| a. Raw strings | `H.halt` entity with `resolved(match)`. Descriptor-typed `EntryFilter` fields. `ModelChoice.agent` removed. |
| b. Fake groups | Ungrouped `on.metric` overload. |
| c. Phase dispatch | `ctx.wait` replaces `until`. `failsTo` replaces `unit.failures` branching. |
| Scenario 4 placement | `Command.on(...runners)`. |

The first pass also made a long list of cuts: `ctx.until`, `ctx.children`, `HaltRequest`, unread view fields, the `on.enters` array form, the `folder.files` `write` option, unread re-exports and the kernel `Recall` types.

### Second pass (scenarios 11 and 12)

| Addition | Scenario need | Why it is not an escape hatch |
|---|---|---|
| `Lane.retry(policy, exhausted)` | 11: EU retries 3× with backoff, US 1×, one kind. | Principle 12 puts the retry policy and its end state on the lane. The required `exhausted` argument makes "bounded and endless" unrepresentable. |
| Position derived from attempt state | 11: forty contracts waiting on counsel hold no WIP and are not active. | Principle 12: waiting on a human is the blocked state, recorded once. The parent counted blocked attempts toward WIP, which broke it. |
| `Halt.about`, `.timeout`, `.policy` | 11: the clock resolver ("approve under $500"), and skipping counsel by a registered policy with recorded reads. | Principle 17's three resolvers, each referencing the halt by identity. |
| `H.on.halted` and the `act.run` effect | 11: page a deputy at 20 minutes from the recorded raise. | Principle 13 lists running an executable as a trigger consequence. |
| `H.ops.resolve(...halts)` | 11: counsel and finance hold disjoint grants. | Principle 17: a grant names the halt. |
| `on.enters(..., { times })` | 11: the second return declines the contract, with no count in the flow. | A declared bound that the kernel enforces. |
| `Supply.deferred` | 11: a redline during `draft` is applied next round; during counsel it re-enters at `draft`. | One flag, resolved by the kernel. |
| `Metrics.median`, `Metrics.count`; measures `decisionMs`, `lockWaitMs`; `EntryFilter.resolver`, `.resource` | 11 and 12 telemetry. | Sample counts stay beside every rate and mean. |
| `H.resource`, `Lane.locks`, `LeaseEntry` | 12: exclusive migrations and shared backfills per database. | Principle 8: the resource is an entity and the lease is ledger state. |
| `Lane.after` and `TransitionEntry.reason` | 12: 0042 waits for 0041, and is parked with a reason if 0041 fails. | Ordering is a lane relationship, not on the kind (principle 10). |
| `H.job` and `JobPoll` | 12: a GPU job polled every 10 minutes, holding no capacity. | Principle 3's external job. Batch remains a separate model-only form; see known weakness 2. |
| `folder.files({ key })` | 12: migration keys come from file names, so `after` can address them. | One option. |

## Principles broken

- **12, partially.** `KindDescriptor.failsTo` lets a kind declare a failure move, which principle 12 now forbids ("the kind declares nothing about failure").
  - It is kept only because scenarios 1–10 of this variant were written against it.
  - `Lane.retry(policy, exhausted)` is the conforming form, and scenarios 11 and 12 use only it.
  - `failsTo` should be deleted when those scenarios migrate.

Everything else holds. The rule that blocked attempts sit at `waiting` replaces the parent's WIP rule, which broke principle 12.

const betweenSamples = H.state('between-samples', 'waiting');
const aWins = H.state('a-wins', 'terminal', 'success');
const bWins = H.state('b-wins', 'terminal', 'success');
const inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const Experiment = H.kind('Experiment')
  .data(z.object({ name: z.string(), endsAt: z.string() }))
  .states(planned, sampling, betweenSamples, aWins, bWins, inconclusive);

const reading = z.object({
  visitorsA: z.number(),
  conversionsA: z.number(),
  visitorsB: z.number(),
  conversionsB: z.number(),
});
type Reading = z.infer<typeof reading>;
type ExperimentResult = 'a-wins' | 'b-wins' | 'inconclusive';

const readExperiment = H.command('read-experiment-metric')
  .input(z.object({ experiment: z.string() }))
  .output(reading)
  .argv((target) => ['experiment-metric', '--name', target.experiment, '--json'])
  .on(local);

const judgeExperiment = H.policy.rule('experiment-verdict', (latest: Reading): ExperimentResult => {
  const visitorsA = Math.max(latest.visitorsA, 1);
  const visitorsB = Math.max(latest.visitorsB, 1);
  const pooled = (latest.conversionsA + latest.conversionsB) / (visitorsA + visitorsB);
  const spread = Math.sqrt(pooled * (1 - pooled) * (1 / visitorsA + 1 / visitorsB));
  if (spread === 0) return 'inconclusive';
  const score = (latest.conversionsA / visitorsA - latest.conversionsB / visitorsB) / spread;
  return score > 1.96 ? 'a-wins' : score < -1.96 ? 'b-wins' : 'inconclusive';
});

const observeExperiment = H.flow('observe-experiment').for(Experiment).does(async (ctx) => {
  const endsAt = new Date(ctx.unit.data.endsAt);
  let latest: Reading | null = null;
  while (ctx.now() < endsAt) {
    await ctx.move('sampling');
    const sample = await ctx.run(readExperiment, { experiment: ctx.unit.data.name });
    if (sample.ok) latest = sample.value;
    await ctx.wait('between-samples', { at: new Date(ctx.now().getTime() + 3_600_000) });
  }
  if (latest === null) return ctx.fail('no metric reading was collected');
  return ctx.decide(judgeExperiment, latest);
});

const collectEval = H.command('collect-eval')
  .input(z.string())
  .output(z.discriminatedUnion('status', [
    z.object({ status: z.literal('running') }),
    z.object({ status: z.literal('done'), result: evalResult }),
    z.object({ status: z.literal('failed'), error: z.string() }),
  ]))
  .argv(jobId => ['gpu', 'status', '--json', jobId])
  .on(local)
  .recovery('rerun');

const gpuEval = H.job('gpu-eval')
  .output(evalResult)
  .submit(submitEval)
  .collect(collectEval, { minutes: 10 });

const scoreEval = H.command('score-eval')
  .input(z.object({ resultsUrl: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ score: z.number() }))
  .argv(input => ['evals', 'score', '--results', input.resultsUrl])
  .on(local)
  .recovery('rerun');

const summarizerRole = H.role('eval-summarizer')
  .input(z.object({ suite: z.string(), score: z.number(), resultsUrl: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Summarize the ${input.suite} evaluation (score ${input.score}) from ${input.resultsUrl} for the team.`);

const summarizer = H.agent('eval-summarizer', summarizerRole).model(anthropic.model('claude-sonnet-4'));

const evalFlow = H.flow('eval-run').for(EvalRun).does(async ctx => {
  const data = ctx.unit.data;
  const prepared = await ctx.run(prepareEval, { checkpoint: data.checkpoint, suite: data.suite });
  if (!prepared.ok) return ctx.fail(prepared.error);
  const job = await ctx.run(gpuEval, { checkpoint: data.checkpoint, suite: data.suite, bundle: prepared.value });
  if (!job.ok) return ctx.fail(job.error);
  const score = await ctx.run(scoreEval, { resultsUrl: job.value.resultsUrl });
  if (!score.ok) return ctx.fail(score.error);
  const summary = await ctx.run(summarizer, { suite: data.suite, score: score.value.score, resultsUrl: job.value.resultsUrl });
  if (!summary.ok) return ctx.fail(summary.error);
  await ctx.update({ score: score.value.score, summary: summary.value.summary });

});

const applyMigration = H.command('apply-migration')
  .input(z.object({ database: databaseName, file: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['migrate', 'apply', '--database', input.database, input.file])
  .on(local)
  .recovery('park');

  const result = await ctx.run(applyMigration, { database: ctx.unit.data.database, file: ctx.unit.data.file });
  if (!result.ok) return ctx.fail(result.error);
  return 'applied';
});

const batchRows = 10_000;

const copyBatch = H.command('copy-backfill-batch')
  .input(z.object({ table: z.string(), database: databaseName, offset: z.number() }))
  .output(z.object({ copied: z.number() }))
  .argv(input => ['backfill', 'batch', '--database', input.database, '--table', input.table, '--offset', String(input.offset), '--limit', String(batchRows)])
  .on(local)
  .recovery('rerun');

const backfillFlow = H.flow('backfill').for(Backfill).does(async ctx => {
  let offset = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const batch = await ctx.run(copyBatch, { table: ctx.unit.data.table, database: ctx.unit.data.database, offset });
    if (!batch.ok) return ctx.fail(batch.error);
    if (batch.value.copied < batchRows) return 'backfilled';
    offset += batchRows;
  }
});

function migrationId(path: string): string {
  return path.split('/').pop()?.slice(0, 4) ?? path;
}

const migrationFiles = folder.files(Migration, {
  dir: 'migrations',
  key: file => migrationId(file.path),
  read: file => {
    const id = migrationId(file.path);
    const number = Number(id);
    return {
      id,
      database: databaseName.parse(file.frontmatter.database),
      file: file.path,
      previous: number > 1 ? String(number - 1).padStart(4, '0') : null,
    };
  },
});

const mlStore = 'ml.db';

const evalTwice = H.policy.retry('eval-twice', view => view.failures < 2 ? { retryInMs: 600_000 } : 'stop');
const neverRetry = H.policy.retry('never-retry', () => 'stop');
const backfillBackoff = H.policy.retry('backfill-backoff', view =>
  view.failures <= 3 ? { retryInMs: 30_000 * 2 ** (view.failures - 1) } : 'stop');

const evalRuns = H.lane('eval-runs', EvalRun)
  .handler(evalFlow)
  .suppliers(H.operator)
  .store(sqlite.store(EvalRun, mlStore))
  .wip(2)
  .retry(evalTwice, 'failed');

const migrations = H.lane('migrations', Migration)
  .handler(migrationFlow)
  .suppliers(migrationFiles)
  .store(migrationFiles)
  .wip(4)
  .retry(neverRetry, 'failed')
  .locks(data => [{ resource: databases[data.database], mode: 'exclusive' }])
  .after(data => data.previous, 'held-by-predecessor');

const backfills = H.lane('backfills', Backfill)
  .handler(backfillFlow)
  .suppliers(H.operator)
  .store(sqlite.store(Backfill, mlStore))
  .wip(4)
  .retry(backfillBackoff, 'failed')
  .locks(data => [{ resource: databases[data.database], mode: 'shared' }]);

const migrationsFirst = H.policy.scheduler('migrations-first', view => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((a, b) => {
    const rank = (unit: typeof a) => (unit.is(Migration) ? 0 : unit.is(Backfill) ? 1 : 2);
    return rank(a) - rank(b) || b.waitedMs - a.waitedMs;
  }),
}));

const pool = H.pool('ml-api', [
  { account: anthropic.account('ml-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 },
]);

export function platformTelemetry(metrics: Metrics) {
  const gpu = metrics.sum({ of: 'durationMs', among: { entry: 'invocation', status: 'ended', executable: gpuEval, mode: 'job' }, days: 1 });
  return {
    gpuJobHoursToday: { hours: gpu.value === null ? null : gpu.value / 3_600_000, samples: gpu.samples },
    lockWaitOrders: metrics.mean({ of: 'lockWaitMs', among: { entry: 'lease', status: 'acquired', resource: databases.orders }, days: 7 }),
    lockWaitBilling: metrics.mean({ of: 'lockWaitMs', among: { entry: 'lease', status: 'acquired', resource: databases.billing }, days: 7 }),
  };
}

export const mlPlatform = H.harness('ml-platform')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('ml-ledger.db'))
  .lanes(evalRuns, migrations, backfills)
  .pools(pool)
  .scheduler(migrationsFirst)
  .clients(claudeCode.supervisor({ grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.writeWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readTelemetry] }))
  .observers(markdown.board('board.md'), markdown.telemetry('telemetry.md'));

# harness-dsl: demand-driven lanes (child of g02-durable-le-1-2-1)

Lens: GenStage / Broadway. Work flows from producers to consumers only as fast as consumers ask for it.

- Suppliers are **producers**.
- Lanes are **consumers** whose demand is their free capacity.
- The scheduler is the **dispatcher**.
- Unit events are **messages**. A message is acknowledged when something has used it, and is never dropped for want of a handler.
- The batch step is the **batcher**.

The owner's vocabulary stays. The lens contributes three rules and one word, *demand*. It adds no new entity except `Loopback`, which the adversary's counsel scenario forced.

| GenStage / Broadway | harness-dsl |
|---|---|
| producer | supplier |
| buffer of produced events | the ledger's pending queue (pending units hold nothing) |
| consumer `max_demand` | lane WIP, runner slots, account eligibility, unit budget, free locks |
| dispatcher | schedule policy, which orders candidates; the kernel grants demand |
| message ack | `SupplySink.emit` resolves with a `SupplyAck` only after the durable append |
| unhandled message stays in mailbox | `event.deferred`; routed later by `event.routed` |
| batcher | `batch` step (cloud batch API, priced `batch`) |
| `demand: :accumulate` (pause) | `lane.paused`: the lane's demand is zero, and running attempts finish |

## Execution vocabulary (one definition each)

- **Unit**: one piece of work of one kind in one lane.
  - Its key is unique in the lane forever, so a second create with the same key is recorded as `unit.deduplicated`.
  - A unit outlives its attempts.
  - It has one state of its kind, and that state's position is the unit's position.
- **Attempt**: one pass of the lane's flow over a unit.
  - Its outcome is succeeded, failed or cancelled.
  - While open, its status is `running` or `blocked`. Blocked means waiting on a human, and `BlockView.reason` says why.
- **Halt**: the flow step that blocks an attempt for a decision.
  - The decision entity (`H.decision`) is what grants, metrics, timers and policies reference.
  - The halt step key is its address in one flow.
- **Step**: one named node of a flow.
- **Invocation**: one execution of an executable inside a step. A retry is a new invocation.
- **Job**: an executable submitted now and collected later.
  - A cloud batch of model calls is a job whose driver is the model's.
  - An `H.job` is a job whose submit and collect are commands.
- **Demand**: the capacity a lane offers right now. It is the minimum of:
  - WIP minus active units;
  - free runner slots;
  - eligible accounts;
  - grantable locks;
  - zero if the lane is paused.

  Demand is folded from the ledger, never stored.

## The three rules of the lens

### Rule 1: capacity follows position, and nothing else

- Only units at an **active** state consume demand.
- A unit at a waiting state holds no WIP, no runner slot and no account, even if its attempt is still open.

**Halt and spawn steps.**
- Every halt key and every spawn key must map to a **waiting** state of the kind.
- When the attempt reaches that step, the unit moves to that state and releases its demand.
- When the decision arrives, or the last child ends, the attempt is queued `resume`.

**Batch and job steps.**
- A batch or job step may map to a waiting state, which releases the slot while the job runs.
- It may also map to an active state, which holds the slot.

**Kernel-caused blocks.**
- These are budget, an exhausted step, an agent question, a restart, or a definition change.
- They move the unit to the lane's optional `blocked:` waiting state.

**The board** reads only the state's position.

### Rule 2: messages are never dropped; unrouted messages are deferred

Every supplied or trigger-sent event is appended as `event.received`. Its routing works like this:

- **Reaction from the current state.** The reaction fires, recorded as `event.routed`.
- **No reaction from the current state, but one elsewhere.** The event is recorded as `event.deferred`. It is re-examined on each state entry, in arrival order, one per append.
- **No reaction anywhere in the lane.** The event is a data message.

Flows that declare `.events({...})` read the unit's whole inbox for those names, typed and in arrival order, frozen at attempt open.

Timers that find no reaction are recorded as `timer.lapsed`, not deferred.

### Rule 3: a producer is acknowledged only after the ledger has the item

`SupplySink.emit` resolves with a `SupplyAck` only after the append. Push adapters answer their sender only after the ack.

## Entities

### Kinds (no backend)

`H.state(name, position[, verdict])`. Terminal states must declare a verdict.

`H.work`: `.attributes`, `.fields`, `.states`, `.events`, `.timers`, `.key`, `.failsTo`.

`H.role`, `H.decision`, `H.memory.experience` and `H.memory.taste` (with `.curated()`), `H.command`, `H.job`.

`H.resource`: a named shared thing (a file pattern, a database, a host). Locks and leases reference it by identity.

`H.flow`: it is blind to kinds and states.

### Instances (adapter subpaths)

Account, model, runner, ledger and its quota partition, store, memory store, supplier, client, projection, external executable.

### Pivots

| Pivot | Composed of | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| lane | kind × suppliers × store × flow × runner × retry × WIP × locks × order | where a kind's units are produced, kept and handled, and the demand they offer |
| agent | role × model or model policy × pool × journals | an executable that thinks |
| pool | accounts × shares × preference × fallback | the accounts an agent may draw on |
| journal | memory kind × memory store × recall policy | where items are written and how they are recalled |
| reaction | target state × source states × cancellation | the routing of a message |
| loopback | return state × maximum × exhausted state | a bounded way back to an earlier state |
| trigger | source × consequences | a recorded firing |
| threshold | metric × group × trip/reset bounds | recorded crossings |
| access | operations × halts it resolves | what a client may do |
| report | metric reads | named readings on telemetry and the control API |
| harness | ledger × lanes × triggers × schedule × clients × projections × reports | a running node (`start`) or a console (`console`) |

## Rules

### Flows are decoupled from kind states

The lane's `states:` map is the only bridge between flow and kind.

| Flow key | Allowed targets | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| step, batch and job keys | any state | optional |
| halt and spawn keys | waiting states | required |
| end labels | non-active states, or a `Loopback` | required |
| `opens` | active states | required when the kind has active states |

### Loopback

`H.loopback(New, { max, then })` is an end-label target. It moves the unit back to `New` at most `max` times over the unit's life, and moves it to `then` on the next occurrence. The count is folded from `unit.transition` facts carrying the label.

### Failure and retry

- A failed attempt returns the unit to pending under the lane's `retry`.
- When the bound is reached, the unit moves to the kind's `failsTo` state.
- With no `.retry`:
  - a kind with `failsTo` gets 0 retries;
  - a kind without one gets unbounded exponential backoff.
- A bounded `.retry` on a kind without `failsTo` is a startup error.
- Two lanes of one kind may declare different retries.

### Outcome rate and track record

- The rate is success / (success + failure) over terminal units, with `n` beside it.
- Neutral endings are counted in `byVerdict`, `byState` and `share`.

### Reactions and cancellation

- A reaction from an active state must say `.cancels()`.
- A reaction from a waiting state with an open attempt may say `.cancels()`. The attempt is then cancelled and the unit re-enters the flow from the top.

### Spawn

- The spawn step maps to a waiting state.
- `child.ended` facts resume the parent when the last child ends.

### Halts: resolvers and clocks

A halt resolution is recorded as `halt.resolved` with `resolver: 'human' | 'policy' | 'timeout'` and `haltedAt`.

**Human.** A client whose access `resolves([decision])` names the halt's decision. Grants name decisions, never strings. The builtin `resolveBlocks` covers kernel blocks only: budget, question, step, restart and definition.

**Policy.** `H.policy.halt(name, kind, decision, decide)` is a registered deterministic function, set in the lane's `resolvers: { haltKey: policy }`.
- It runs when the halt is reached.
- A non-null result resolves the halt with that value. The resolution is recorded as `policy.decided`, with its metric reads and sample counts, and then `halt.resolved` with `resolver: 'policy'`.
- A null result leaves the halt to the other resolvers.

**Clock.** `halt(key, decision, { ask, timeout: { after, resolve } })` resolves the halt itself when no one has answered `after` the recorded `halt.opened`, with `resolver: 'timeout'`.
- The attempt continues; nothing is cancelled.
- The deadline is stored on `halt.opened`, so it survives restarts and never reads unit data.

**Paging before the clock.** `H.on.halted(decision, { after })` is a trigger source. It fires once per halt still unresolved `after` its recorded opening. Typical use: paging a deputy. Anyone the access names may resolve.

### Jobs

`H.job(name, { submit, collect, poll, status })` is an executable used with the ordinary `.step`.

**Submit.**
- The kernel runs `submit` once and parses `{ jobId }`.
- It appends `job.submitted`, then releases the slot if the step maps to a waiting state.

**Collect.**
- Every `poll`, the kernel runs `collect` on a briefly acquired slot of the lane's runner, with `HARNESS_JOB_ID` in its environment.
- `status(data)` returns `running`, `succeeded` or `failed`.
- `failed` is an invocation failure, so the attempt fails.

**Restart.**
- A recorded `job.submitted` means collect resumes; the job is never resubmitted.
- A crash between submit and its record follows the step's restart rule, `escalate` by default.

**Batches.** A cloud batch is the same fact with `sort: 'batch'`.

**Metrics.** `metrics.jobs` folds hours in flight from submission to collection, with `n`.

### Locks on resources

`lane.locks(unit => [{ resource, mode }])` declares locks.
- A unit is a candidate only if all its locks are grantable.
  - An exclusive lock excludes every other lock.
  - A shared lock excludes exclusive locks.
- Locks are acquired at attempt start as a lease on the ledger (`lock.acquired`, carrying `waitedMs` from readiness).
- They are released at attempt end.
- While the attempt is blocked or waiting the lock is kept, because it protects data, not capacity.

File-write leases are the same mechanism, in exclusive mode keyed by path.

`metrics.lockWait` reports wait time per resource with `n`.

### Ordering between units

`lane.after(unit => predecessorKey | null, parksIn)` makes a unit a candidate only once the predecessor unit in the same lane has reached a terminal success state.
- It applies whatever order the units were supplied in. A missing predecessor simply waits.
- A predecessor ending in a failure or neutral terminal state moves the unit to `parksIn`, a waiting state. The cause is `{ by: 'order', ref: '<key> ended in <state>' }`, shown on the board.

### Batch-shaped resumption

A `loop` body's steps are recorded per round. After a crash, recorded rounds replay at no cost, and the round that was running follows its restart rule. A backfill with `restart: 'rerun'` on its batch command therefore resumes at the interrupted batch, never at the first. The author writes no checkpoint.

### Metrics and reports

- Metrics are as before: `{ rate, hits, n, window }`.
- Windows are a `Duration`, `'all'` or `{ sinceMs }`.
- `MetricQuery.resolver` filters decision metrics.
- `metrics.decisions` gives median time to decision per halt, filtered by resolver, with `n`, counts per resolver, and `share(resolver)`.
- `metrics.attempts(...).retries` counts retry attempts.
- `H.report(name, read)` is a deterministic function from metrics to named readings. A reading is a number, a rate or a stat, each with `n`. Reports are published on telemetry projections and via `readTelemetry`.

### Restart after a crash

The author writes only restart rules and probes.

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `rerun` | runs the step again |
| `escalate` (default for commands, externals and an unrecorded job submit) | blocks the attempt with reason `restart` |
| `ask` (default for agents) | `Driver.settled` / `External.settled` reports whether the invocation finished |
| `{ probe }` | runs the probe command |

- Jobs resume collection from `job.submitted`.
- Halts resolved while the harness was down, and children that ended, are ledger facts.
- A resumed attempt keeps its id.
- A changed fingerprint prefix blocks the attempt with reason `definition`.
- A fenced writer lease ensures a single writer.

### Accounts and quota

- `Ledger.quota` is an append-only `QuotaPartition`.
- `sqlite.quota(shared)` places it in a file both harnesses name.

### Control API

- Operations and resolvable halts are granted through an access.
- Transport is the client adapter.

### Startup validation

`start()` fails on any of:
- duplicate names;
- a halt or spawn key mapped to a non-waiting state;
- an end label mapped to an active state;
- a kind with active states but no `opens`;
- a reaction from an active state without `.cancels()`;
- a reaction or loopback state outside the kind;
- a flow event the kind lacks;
- a bounded `.retry` on a kind without `failsTo`;
- an unregistered lane in `unit()` / `event()` / `pauses()`;
- a terminal state without a verdict;
- `restart: 'ask'` on an executable with no `settled`;
- a batch on a model that cannot batch;
- an agent without a model or pool;
- `.sets` keys that are fields;
- a halt resolver policy whose decision differs from the halt's;
- a halt no access resolves that has neither a timeout nor a resolver policy;
- an `after` parking state that is not waiting.

## What changed and why

**Lens generation (versus parent).**
- Capacity follows position.
- Deferred routing of messages.
- `SupplyAck`.
- Pause is zero demand.
- `.mark` is removed, and the lane maps step keys to states.
- `H.loopback` is added.
- `failsTo` replaces the `parked` flag.
- `event.deferred` / `event.routed` / `timer.lapsed` are added, and `child.ended` replaces `monitor.down`.
- `H.on.event` is removed.

**Scenarios 11 and 12 (run two).**
- **Halt clock.** The halt spec gains `timeout: { after, resolve }`. `halt.opened` carries the deadline. `halt.resolved` carries `resolver` and `haltedAt`, and `DecisionFact` gains `resolver` and `waitedMs`. Without these, a timeout could only cancel.
- **Paging before the clock.** `H.on.halted(decision, { after })` and `HaltEvent` are added, so the 20-minute deputy page is a recorded trigger measured from the halt.
- **Policy resolvers.**
  - `H.policy.halt` and the kernel's `HaltPolicy` replace the inline `Skip` object, and the lane config key `skips` becomes `resolvers`.
  - Reason: scenario 11 requires the skip to be a registered policy whose decision records its metric reads. The old skip was an anonymous predicate whose results were never decision samples.
  - Scenario 2 rewrites its one `skips:` line as `resolvers: { approval: H.policy.halt(...) }`.
- **Scoped resolvers.** `Access.resolves(decisions)` and `AccessSpec.resolves` are added. `resolveBlocks` now covers kernel blocks only.
- **Jobs.**
  - `H.job` and the kernel's `JobSpec` are added. `Executable` gains the `'job'` sort.
  - `batch.submitted` is generalized to `job.submitted { sort: 'batch' | 'job' }`, and `InvocationView.batchId` becomes `jobId`.
  - This partly answers known weakness 2: one fact and one restart rule for both batches and jobs, though the batch step keeps its own builder because it fans out items.
- **Locks.**
  - `lane.locks` and `LockRequest` are added, with `lock.acquired` / `lock.released` facts.
  - `Ledger.lease` takes `{ key, mode }` claims, so file leases and database locks are one mechanism.
  - Grantable locks join demand.
- **Ordering.** `lane.after(predecessor, parksIn)` is added, and `Cause.by` gains `'order'`.
- **Metrics.**
  - `Window` gains `{ sinceMs }`, for "this month".
  - `MetricQuery.resolver` is added.
  - `metrics.decisions`, `metrics.jobs`, `metrics.lockWait` and `AttemptCounts.retries` are added.
- **Reports.** `H.report` and `harness.reports` are added. Medians, hours in flight and lock waits are not rates, and nothing could publish them before.
- **Adapter.** `harness-dsl/ironclad` provides a document-system store.

## Principles broken

none.

`lane.after` and `lane.locks` put relationships on the lane, never on the kind (principle 10). Resources and decisions are referenced by identity (principle 8).

  type Waiting<St> = Extract<St, { readonly position: 'waiting' }>;

  type SettledState<St extends State> = Extract<Settled<St>, State>;

  export type External<I, O> = K.External<I, O>;

  export interface Command<D = null> extends K.Executable<K.CommandInput, K.CommandResult<D>>, K.CommandSpec {

  export interface Agent<I, O> extends K.Executable<I, O> {
    readonly executable: 'agent';
    readonly role: Role<I, O>;
    model(model: K.Model | K.ChoicePolicy<K.Model>): Agent<I, O>;
    pool(pool: Pool | K.Account): Agent<I, O>;
    recalls(journals: readonly Journal[]): Agent<I, O>;
    records(journal: Journal): Agent<I, O>;

    mustPass(check: K.CommandSpec): Agent<I, O>;
  }

  export interface Retry extends K.RetrySpec { readonly entity: 'retry' }

  export type Restart = 'rerun' | 'ask' | 'escalate' | { readonly probe: Command<{ readonly done: boolean }> };

  export interface StepOptions {
    readonly retry?: Retry;
    readonly timeoutMs?: number;
    readonly onFailure?: 'fail' | 'halt';
    readonly runner?: K.Runner;
    readonly restart?: Restart;
  }

  export interface FlowContext<In, P, Out, Ev> {
    readonly input: In;
    readonly params: P;
    readonly out: Out;
    readonly events: { readonly [N in keyof Ev]: readonly K.Received<Ev[N]>[] };
    readonly unit: K.UnitView;
    readonly attempt: K.AttemptView;
  }
  export interface LoopRound<C> { readonly round: number; readonly carry: C | null }
  type Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X> = FlowContext<In, P, Out, Ev> & X;

  export interface Flow<In, P, Out, Sp, Sk extends string, L extends string, Ev, Hl, Wt extends string> extends K.FlowSpec {
    readonly entity: 'flow';
    readonly types?: { input: In; params: P; out: Out; spawns: Sp; steps: Sk; ends: L; events: Ev; halts: Hl; waits: Wt };
  }

  export interface FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, Sk extends string, L extends string, Ev, Hl, Wt extends string, X> extends K.Named {
    readonly entity: 'flow-draft';
    requires<S extends Shape>(shape: S): FlowDraft<Obj<S>, P, Out, Sp, Sk, L, Ev, Hl, Wt, X>;
    params<S extends Shape>(shape: S): FlowDraft<In, Obj<S>, Out, Sp, Sk, L, Ev, Hl, Wt, X>;
    events<E extends { [name: string]: Shape }>(events: E): FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, Sk, L, { [N in keyof E]: Obj<E[N]> }, Hl, Wt, X>;
    step<Q extends string, I, O>(
      key: Q,
      executable: K.Executable<I, O>,
      input: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => NoInfer<I>,
      options?: StepOptions,
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: O }, Sp, Sk | Q, L, Ev, Hl, Wt, X>;
    batch<Q extends string, I, O>(
      key: Q,
      agent: Agent<I, O>,
      items: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => readonly NoInfer<I>[],
      options?: StepOptions,
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: readonly O[] }, Sp, Sk | Q, L, Ev, Hl, Wt, X>;
    halt<Q extends string, D>(
      key: Q,
      decision: Decision<D>,
      spec: {
        ask: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => string;
        timeout?: { after: K.Duration; resolve: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => NoInfer<D> };
      },
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: D }, Sp, Sk, L, Ev, Hl & { [R in Q]: D }, Wt | Q, X>;
    spawn<Q extends string, O extends string, S extends Shape>(
      key: Q,
      spec: { outlet: O; child: S; items: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => readonly Obj<S>[] },
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: readonly K.ChildView[] }, Sp & { [R in O]: Obj<S> }, Sk, L, Ev, Hl, Wt | Q, X>;
    loop<Q extends string, C extends Shape, B, Sk2 extends string, Hl2, Wt2 extends string>(
      key: Q,
      spec: { carry: C; rounds: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => number },
      body: (round: FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, Sk, L, Ev, Hl, Wt, X & LoopRound<Obj<C>>>) => FlowDraft<In, P, B, Sp, Sk2, L, Ev, Hl2, Wt2, X & LoopRound<Obj<C>>>,
      again: (last: B, c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => Obj<C> | null,
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: { rounds: number; last: B; exhausted: boolean } }, Sp, Sk2, L, Ev, Hl2, Wt2, X>;
    sets<S extends ScalarShape>(shape: S, make: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => Obj<S>): FlowDraft<In & Obj<S>, P, Out, Sp, Sk, L, Ev, Hl, Wt, X>;
    exit<E extends string>(label: E, when: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => boolean): FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, Sk, L | E, Ev, Hl, Wt, X>;
    ends<E extends string>(labels: readonly E[], pick: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => NoInfer<E>): Flow<In, P, Out, Sp, Sk, L | E, Ev, Hl, Wt>;
  }

  export interface Reaction<To extends State, Fr extends State = never> extends K.ReactionSpec {
    readonly entity: 'reaction';
    readonly to: To;
    readonly fromStates: readonly Fr[];
    from<S extends State>(states: readonly S[]): Reaction<To, Fr | S>;
    cancels(): Reaction<To, Fr>;
  }

  export interface Loopback<To extends State, Th extends State> extends K.LoopbackSpec {
    readonly entity: 'loopback';
    readonly to: To;
    readonly then: Th;
  }

  type EndTarget<St extends State> = Settled<St> | Loopback<SettledState<St>, SettledState<St>>;

  type HandlerConfig<A, F, St extends State, Ev, In, P, Sp, Sk extends string, L extends string, FEv, Hl, Wt extends string> =
    { states: { [Q in L]: EndTarget<St> } & { [Q in Wt]: Waiting<St> } & { [Q in Sk]?: St } } &
    ([Active<St>] extends [never] ? {} : { opens: Active<St> }) &
    { blocked?: Waiting<St> } &
    ({} extends P ? { params?: P } : { params: P }) &
    ({} extends Sp ? {} : { spawns: { [Q in keyof Sp]: (child: Sp[Q]) => K.NewUnit } }) &
    { resolvers?: { [Q in keyof Hl]?: K.HaltPolicy<A, Hl[Q]> } } &
    ([A & F] extends [In] ? {} : { unitDoesNotSatisfyFlowInput: never }) &
    ([Ev] extends [FEv] ? {} : { kindLacksFlowEvents: never });

  export interface Lane<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, Out> extends K.LaneLike<A> {
    readonly entity: 'lane';
    readonly types?: { attributes: A; fields: F; state: St; events: Ev; timers: Tm; out: Out };
    supply(suppliers: readonly K.Supplier<K.Supply<A, F, Ev>>[]): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    store(store: K.Store): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    handler<In, P, O, Sp, Sk extends string, L extends string, FEv, Hl, Wt extends string>(
      flow: Flow<In, P, O, Sp, Sk, L, FEv, Hl, Wt>,
      config: NoInfer<HandlerConfig<A, F, St, Ev, In, P, Sp, Sk, L, FEv, Hl, Wt>>,
    ): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, O>;
    runner(runner: K.Runner): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    preflight(check: K.CommandSpec): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    wip(max: number): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    retry(policy: Retry): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    budget(budget: { maxUsdPerUnit: number; onExceed: 'halt' | 'fail' }): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    locks(make: (unit: { attributes: A }) => readonly K.LockRequest[]): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    after(predecessor: (unit: { key: string; attributes: A }) => string | null, parksIn: Waiting<St>): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    reacts(reactions: { [N in (keyof Ev & string) | Tm]?: Reaction<St, St> }): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Out>;
    unit(create: K.Create<A, F>): K.NewUnit;
    event<N extends keyof Ev & string>(key: string, name: N, payload: Ev[N]): K.UnitEvent;
  }

  export interface Source<E> {
    readonly entity: 'source';
    readonly types?: { event: E };
  }

  export interface Trigger<E> extends K.TriggerSpec {
    where(test: (event: E) => boolean): Trigger<E>;
    creates(make: (event: E) => K.NewUnit | readonly K.NewUnit[]): Trigger<E>;
    sends(make: (event: E) => K.UnitEvent | readonly K.UnitEvent[]): Trigger<E>;
    records(journal: Journal, make: (event: E) => readonly K.MemoryDraft[]): Trigger<E>;
    invokes<I, O>(executable: K.Executable<I, O>, make: (event: E) => NoInfer<I>): Trigger<E>;
    pauses(lane: K.LaneLike<unknown>): Trigger<E>;
    resumes(lane: K.LaneLike<unknown>): Trigger<E>;
  }

  export interface Metric extends K.MetricSpec { readonly entity: 'metric' }
  export interface MetricHit<T extends unknown[]> { hit(test: (...args: T) => boolean): Metric }
  export interface MetricDraft {
    of<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, O>(lane: Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, O>): MetricHit<[event: K.TransitionEvent<A, O>]>;
    of<D>(decision: Decision<D>): MetricHit<[decision: D, fact: K.DecisionFact]>;
    of<I, O>(executable: K.Executable<I, O>): MetricHit<[output: O, invocation: K.InvocationView]>;
    invocations(sorts?: readonly K.InvocationView['sort'][]): MetricHit<[invocation: K.InvocationView]>;
  }

  export interface ThresholdSpec {
    readonly window: K.Duration;
    readonly minSamples: number;
    readonly trips: K.Bound;
    readonly resets: K.Bound;
  }
  export interface Threshold<G> extends K.ThresholdRule {
    readonly entity: 'threshold';
    readonly types?: { group: G };
  }

  export interface HaltPolicyDraft<A, D> extends K.Named {
    decides(decide: (c: K.GateContext<A>) => D | null): K.HaltPolicy<A, D>;
  }

  export interface Operation extends K.OperationSpec { readonly entity: 'operation' }
  export interface OperationDraft<I> extends K.Named {
    input<S extends Shape>(shape: S): OperationDraft<Obj<S>>;
    invokes<EI, EO>(executable: K.Executable<EI, EO>, prepare: (input: I) => NoInfer<EI>): Operation;
  }

  export interface Access extends K.AccessSpec {
    readonly entity: 'access';
    allows(operations: readonly Operation[]): Access;
    resolves(decisions: readonly K.DecisionSpec[]): Access;
  }

  export interface Harness extends K.Named {
    readonly entity: 'harness';
    ledger(ledger: K.Ledger): Harness;
    lanes(lanes: readonly K.LaneLike<unknown>[]): Harness;
    triggers(triggers: readonly K.TriggerSpec[]): Harness;
    schedule(policy: K.SchedulePolicy): Harness;
    clients(clients: readonly K.Client[]): Harness;
    projections(projections: readonly K.Projection[]): Harness;
    reports(reports: readonly K.ReportSpec[]): Harness;
    start(): Promise<K.Running>;
    console(): Promise<K.Console>;
  }

  export const H: {
    env(name: string): K.EnvRef;
    slot: { port(index: number): K.PortRef };

    state: {
      <N extends string, P extends 'pending' | 'active' | 'waiting'>(name: N, position: P): State<N, P>;
      <N extends string>(name: N, position: 'terminal', verdict: K.Verdict): State<N, 'terminal'>;
    };
    work(name: string): WorkKind;
    role(name: string): Role;
    resource(name: string): Resource;
    decision<S extends Shape>(name: string, shape: S): Decision<Obj<S>>;
    memory: { experience(name: string): MemoryKind; taste(name: string): MemoryKind };

    command(name: string, argv: readonly string[]): Command;
    job<C>(name: string, spec: {
      submit: Command<{ jobId: string }>;
      collect: Command<C>;
      poll: K.Duration;
      status: (data: NoInfer<C>) => K.JobStatus;
    }): Job<C>;
    agent<I, O>(name: string, role: Role<I, O>): Agent<I, O>;
    pool(name: string): Pool;
    journal(name: string, kind: MemoryKind): Journal;
    retry: {
      exponential(spec: { maxRetries: number; initialDelayMs: number; maxDelayMs?: number }): Retry;
      fixed(spec: { maxRetries: number; delayMs: number }): Retry;
    };

    time: {
      every(interval: K.Duration): K.Recurrence;
      daily(at: string, timeZone?: string): K.Recurrence;
      weekly(day: K.Weekday, at: string, timeZone?: string): K.Recurrence;
      monthly(dayOfMonth: number, at: string, timeZone?: string): K.Recurrence;
    };

    flow(name: string): FlowDraft<{}, {}, {}, {}, never, never, {}, {}, never, {}>;
    lane<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string>(name: string, kind: WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm>): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, {}>;
    reaction<To extends State>(to: To): Reaction<To>;
    loopback<To extends State, Th extends State>(to: To, spec: { max: number; then: Th }): Loopback<To, Th>;

    supply: {
      operator(): K.Supplier<never>;
      schedule<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string>(
        kind: WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm>,
        when: K.Recurrence,
        make: (c: K.ScheduleSupplyContext<A>, supply: K.SupplyMaker<A, F, Ev>) => readonly NoInfer<K.Supply<A, F, Ev>>[],
      ): K.Supplier<K.Supply<A, F, Ev>>;
    };

    on: {
      transition<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, O>(
        lane: Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, O>,
        filter?: { to?: readonly NoInfer<St>[]; from?: readonly NoInfer<St>[]; verdict?: readonly K.Verdict[]; position?: readonly K.Position[] },
      ): Source<K.TransitionEvent<A, O>>;
      streak<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, O>(
        lane: Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, O>,
        spec: { verdict: K.Verdict; count: number; per: keyof NoInfer<A> & string },
      ): Source<K.StreakEvent<A>>;
      step<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, O, Q extends keyof O & string>(
        lane: Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, O>,
        key: Q,
      ): Source<K.StepEvent<A, O[Q]>>;
      halted<D>(decision: Decision<D>, spec: { after: K.Duration }): Source<K.HaltEvent>;
      crossed<G>(threshold: Threshold<G>): Source<K.ThresholdEvent<G>>;
      recovered<G>(threshold: Threshold<G>): Source<K.ThresholdEvent<G>>;
    };
    trigger<E>(name: string, source: Source<E>): Trigger<E>;

    metric(name: string): MetricDraft;
    threshold: {
      <A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, G extends keyof A & string>(
        name: string,
        metric: Metric,
        spec: ThresholdSpec & { kind: WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm>; per: G },
      ): Threshold<Pick<A, G>>;
      (name: string, metric: Metric, spec: ThresholdSpec): Threshold<{}>;
    };
    report(name: string, read: (c: K.ReportContext) => K.Report): K.ReportSpec;

    policy: {
      schedule(name: string, decide: (c: K.ScheduleContext) => K.ScheduleDecision): K.SchedulePolicy;
      model(name: string, options: readonly K.Model[], decide: (c: K.PolicyContext, options: readonly K.Model[]) => K.Model): K.ChoicePolicy<K.Model>;
      account(name: string, decide: (c: K.AccountContext) => K.AccountView | null): K.AccountPolicy;
      recall(name: string, decide: (c: K.RecallContext) => readonly K.RecallCandidate[]): K.RecallPolicy;
      halt<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, D>(
        name: string,
        kind: WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm>,
        decision: Decision<D>,
      ): HaltPolicyDraft<A, D>;
    };

    ops: {
      readonly readWork: Operation;
      readonly createWork: Operation;
      readonly updateWork: Operation;
      readonly sendEvents: Operation;
      readonly resolveBlocks: Operation;
      readonly manageAttempts: Operation;
      readonly readMemory: Operation;
      readonly writeMemory: Operation;
      readonly curateMemory: Operation;
      readonly readTelemetry: Operation;
      readonly readAccounts: Operation;
      readonly setShares: Operation;
    };
    operation(name: string): OperationDraft<{}>;
    access(name: string): Access;

    harness(name: string): Harness;
  };
}
